name: Chitwan National Park Safari
sub_region: Chitwan District, Bagmati Province (park also extends into Makwanpur, Parsa and Nawalparasi)

difficulty.notes: Jeep safari, dugout canoe and guided jungle walks; walks are on flat terrain but in heat and with wildlife risk.

duration_days.basis: 3 days / 2 nights, Kathmandu to Kathmandu (or onward to Pokhara/Lumbini)
duration_days.notes: 2 nights is the common minimum; 3 nights allows a full-day jeep safari toward Kasara and birding at Bis Hajar Tal. Usually combined with Kathmandu and Pokhara in a classic Nepal tour.

itinerary.route: Kathmandu - Bharatpur (flight, ~25-30 min) or road (~5-7 h) - Sauraha; Tharu village walk, Rapti riverside sunset, Tharu stick dance
Dawn dugout canoe on the Rapti - guided jungle walk - Elephant Breeding Centre - afternoon jeep safari
itinerary.notes: Midday heat is usually spent resting at the lodge.

itinerary.route: Optional early birding walk - Bharatpur - Kathmandu (flight) or drive to Pokhara / Lumbini

best_seasons.notes: NTB: Oct-Mar average ~25 C; Apr-Jun hot (up to 43 C); Jul-Sep rainy. Birdwatching best Oct-Mar.

permits.name: Chitwan National Park entry permit
permits.fee: NPR 2,000 per person per day/entry (NTB heritage table adds +13% VAT)
permits.applies_to: foreign nationals; SAARC NPR 1,000; Nepali NPR 150; under 10 free

guide_requirements: Activities inside the park (jungle walks, canoe, jeep safari) are done with licensed nature guides; walking in the park between sunset and sunrise is prohibited by park regulations.

drives: Kathmandu - Sauraha ~165-185 km, 5-7 h via Mugling/Narayangarh
logistics.notes: Park HQ is at Kasara, 21 km from Bharatpur; most visitors base in Sauraha on the park's northern edge.

highlights: Greater one-horned rhinoceros: 694 of Nepal's 752 rhinos counted in Chitwan and adjoining areas (National Rhino Count 2021)
Bengal tiger: an estimated 128 tigers in Chitwan and adjoining forests (2022 national tiger survey; Nepal total 355)
Gharial and mugger crocodiles from a dugout canoe on the Rapti
Tharu village life and stick dance
Nepal's first national park and a natural UNESCO World Heritage Site
risks: Wildlife encounters on foot (rhino, elephant, sloth bear, tiger)
unverified: 13% VAT on the Chitwan park fee is listed on the NTB heritage-fee page but not on the NTB park-fee page or the park's own regulations page.

Elephant-back safaris have declined sharply on welfare grounds (around 45 elephants still used in Sauraha in 2025) but have not been officially banned; OutdoorKing should not offer them (policy choice, not regulation).
Chitwan being Nepal's first/oldest national park is from Kathmandu Post wording; designation year not independently checked.
